name: Roing
description: District headquarters of Lower Dibang Valley, a scenic plain town at the foothills of the Mishmi Hills serving as the main base for exploring the region's lakes, wildlife, forts, and hill passes. Known for orange orchards and as a commercial hub for the area.
facts: Headquarters of Lower Dibang Valley district
Base for visits to Mehao Lake, Mayodia Pass, and Bhishmaknagar Fort
Home to Idu Mishmi and Adi communities; Reh festival celebrated in February

name: Mehao Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Protected area of 281.5 sq km established in 1980 around Mehao Lake, featuring virgin tropical evergreen to temperate forests rich in orchids, birds, and rare mammals including clouded leopards, red pandas, and Mishmi takin.
facts: Home to over 200 bird species, rare orchids, and endemic Mishmi Hills hoolock gibbon subspecies
Includes Mehao Lake and parts of Dibang Wildlife Sanctuary influences
Best visited October to March; about 17 km from Roing

name: Anini
description: Remote district headquarters of Dibang Valley, perched on a plateau between the Dri and Mathun rivers at about 1,968 m elevation. Gateway to high-altitude treks, Idu Mishmi villages, and pristine Mishmi Hills wilderness near the Indo-China border.
facts: Headquarters of Dibang Valley district; northernmost district HQ in Northeast India
Elevation approximately 1,968 metres; population small, primarily Idu Mishmi
Base for Seven Lakes Trek and exploration of Dri and Mathun valleys
Accessible via long drive from Roing (Lower Dibang Valley) over Mayodia Pass; ILP required
